questions.q: When did David sing the song that Yahweh was his rock?
questions.a: David sang the song on the day Yahweh delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul.

questions.q: When David calls on Yahweh, what does he say that Yahweh does?
questions.a: David says when he calls on Yahweh, he is saved from his enemies.

questions.q: What did David feel like when he was surrounded by his enemies?
questions.a: David felt like the waves of death and the cords of Sheol surrounded him.

questions.q: How did David respond to his distressing circumstances?
questions.a: In his distress, David called to Yahweh, and Yahweh heard his voice from his temple.

questions.q: What happened because God was angry?
questions.a: The earth shook and trembled, smoke went up from his nose, and a stream of fire was flowing out from his mouth to burn up everything in its path.

questions.q: How did Yahweh come down from the heavens?
questions.a: He lowered the heavens and came down, riding on a cherub and flying on the wings of the wind.

questions.q: How did Yahweh scatter his enemies?
questions.a: Yahweh thundered from the heavens, sent out arrows and flashes of lightning, and panicked them.

questions.q: How were the foundations of the world uncovered?
questions.a: The foundations of the world were uncovered at the rebuke of Yahweh, from the blast of the breath of his nose.

questions.q: How did Yahweh rescue David from the strong enemy who hated him?
questions.a: David said it was as if Yahweh reached down from heaven and grabbed him so that he could pull David up out of the deep water of the ocean.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh deliver David?
questions.a: Yahweh delivered David because he delighted in him.

questions.q: How did David keep the ways of Yahweh?
questions.a: David kept the ways of Yahweh and did not turn away from his statutes.

questions.q: What happened because David was blameless and kept himself from iniquity?
questions.a: Yahweh gave back to him according to his righteousness and his cleanness.

questions.q: What does Yahweh do to the proud?
questions.a: Yahweh is aware of people who are arrogant, and he humiliates them.

questions.q: What is Yahweh to everyone who takes refuge in him?
questions.a: Yahweh is a shield to all who take refuge in him.

questions.q: Why did David say God was his rock and fortress?
questions.a: David said God was his rock, the only real God, because God is where he can go to be safe. He said God was his fortress of strength because, to David, God is like a very secure place where he could go to hide from danger.

questions.q: Why had David’s feet not slipped?
questions.a: David says that God gave him many ways to respond to each situation, so that his enemies were not able to trap him.

questions.q: What did David do to his enemies when they looked for a savior?
questions.a: David defeated them so completely that they were no longer any threat to him no more than tiny particles of dust would be.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do for David?
questions.a: Yahweh rescued David from the disputes of his people and kept him as the head of nations.

questions.q: What did Yahweh do on behalf of David?
questions.a: Yahweh enabled David to conquer enemies, protecting him from being captured by them. Yahweh kept David safe when people rebelled against him and rescued hm from men who tried to harm him.

questions.q: Why did David sing praises to the name of Yahweh?
questions.a: David said he thanks Yahweh so that all people groups will know that Yahweh is the one who has helped him. He sings to praise Yahweh for the great things he has done, faithfully showing kindness to David and to his descendants in the future.

commentary.text: —This chapter is a psalm of praise; we find it afterwards nearly as Ps 18. They that trust God in the way of duty, shall find him a present help in their greatest dangers: David did so. Remarkable preservations should be particularly mentioned in our praises. We shall never be delivered from all enemies till we get to heaven. God will preserve all his people, 2Ti 4:18. Those who receive signal mercies from God, ought to give him the glory. In the day that God delivered David, he sang this song. While the mercy is fresh, and we are most affected with it, let the thank-offering be brought, to be kindled with the fire of that affection. All his joys and hopes close, as all our hopes should do, in the great Redeemer.
